Ghost Pipes - I find these growing on russula patches

I posted this yesterday in v/nature but I'll put it up again. This is a parasitic plant that I find growing on russula patches around the dismal swamp. Here's some info on them. People also call them Indian pipes.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monotropa_uniflora

Unlike most plants, it is white and does not contain chlorophyll. Instead of generating energy from sunlight, it is parasitic, more specifically a mycoheterotroph. Its hosts are certain fungi that are mycorrhizal with trees, meaning it ultimately gets its energy from photosynthetic trees. Since it is not dependent on sunlight to grow, it can grow in very dark environments as in the understory of dense forest. It is often associated with beech trees.[2] The complex relationship that allows this plant to grow also makes propagation difficult.

Its hosts are certain fungi that are mycorrhizal with trees, meaning it ultimately gets its energy from photosynthetic trees.

So it's a parasite of a parasite (mycorrhiza is a symbiotic relationship but technically still parasitic as the mushroom is living on or inside the plant's roots. Parasitism is not harmful by default).

Yes, it uses the mycelial network of the russula mushrooms to transfer nutrients from the trees to itself. For years I thought it was a type of fungus until I posted some pictures I took to a mycology forum and got yelled at. It's also used by native Americans for medicinal purposes.
